checkResults.evidence: pnpm --dir services/wlt test: 17/17 Node tests pass (openapi composition/bundle/provenance, currency formatting) plus `cd backend && go test ./...` across all 18 Go packages (cod, commercial, http, ledger, payment, payout, reconciliation, reference, refund, settlement, wallet, etc.), all PASS, run against the real Postgres runtime (wlt_runtime on localhost:55432). New/changed test coverage exercised: internal/provider (financial_rail_router_test.go -- production fails closed with no mock/sandbox fallback, mock mode routes correctly, registry maintenance/missing-provider fail closed), internal/reference (topup_session_db_test.go -- purpose derivation, replay, amount-conflict), internal/payment (topup_db_test.go -- authorize/capture DB flow, atomic wallet-credit ledger posting, non-topup-session rejection, ambiguous-provider-error reconciliation-case opening), internal/refund (governed_refund_durable_completion_db_test.go -- new TestCompleteGovernedRefundWithProvider_CodCollectedSourceBlockedFromRail proving the source-aware guard, plus the full pre-existing TestGovernedRefundRuntime* suite re-verified against the CashInRail-shaped fake). Re-run a second time with `go test ./... -count=1` (bypassing Go's test cache entirely) as part of the Freeze adversarial pass: this surfaced and led to fixing a real defect -- see deviations.

grep -rn -E "financial/card/|CashInRail|ProviderRegistry|FinancialRailRouter|mock|sandbox|production" services/wlt/backend/internal (rg substituted, see VERIFICATION.json deviation). Remaining /financial/card/* literals are confined to: (1) provider/financial_rail_router.go's own private path constants (the rail's internal transport detail, not caller-visible), (2) their own tests, (3) internal/payment/payment.go's authorizeProvider/captureProvider and provider_refresh.go -- the pre-existing, unchanged order-payment card flow, out of this unit's scope (T002 targeted the official-wallet Cash-In/topup edge specifically, not order payments). The refund package (governed_refund.go) no longer contains any /financial/card/refund literal at all -- CompleteGovernedRefundWithProvider now calls rail.Refund(...) exclusively. ProviderRegistry (services/wlt/backend/internal/provider/registry.go, pre-existing) is now actually wired into FinancialRailRouter's optional activation check (previously dead code -- registry lookups were unreachable because NewClient was only ever constructed with reg=nil). CashInRail/FinancialRailRouter are the sole types with capability-checked Authorize/Capture/Refund/Status methods; no other package defines a competing rail abstraction. mock/sandbox/production are exclusively selected via provider.Config.Mode (env WLT_FINANCIAL_PROVIDER_MODE), unchanged from pre-existing LoadConfig/NewPaymentProvider, which was already proven (and remains proven by TestFinancialRailRouter_ProductionFailsClosedNoFallback) to refuse construction entirely for ModeProduction -- no mock/sandbox fallback path exists.

pnpm run runtime:wlt:migrate: PASS, files=76, applied wlt-911 (adds topup_reference/topup_actor_type columns, extends the source-XOR and financial_purpose CHECK constraints; zero existing rows affected since no historical session had a topup source). pnpm run runtime:wlt:smoke: PASS -- Identity API healthy, WLT API ready.

pnpm run runtime:financial-simulators: PASS (wiremock-financial-provider container healthy). pnpm run runtime:wlt:provider:smoke: BLOCKED by a pre-existing environment gap unrelated to this unit's changes -- see VERIFICATION.json's knownEnvironmentBlocker field. The currently deployed wlt-api-runtime container is started with a nil wallet.DecisionService (services/wlt/backend/cmd/wlt-api/main.go:52, not modified by this unit), which internal/wallet/circuit_breaker.go's EnforceKillSwitch fails closed on for every financial mutation -- confirmed by observing the smoke script's very first call (an unrelated, pre-existing order-payment session creation) already returning 403 KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE before any topup/refund-specific code executes. This blocks HTTP-level end-to-end verification of the wiremock request journal for every unit in this package, not something U002 introduced. The behavior this check exists to prove (one financial effect per success/failure/ambiguous-result scenario, correct reconciliation state) is instead proven at the Go-test layer against real Postgres: see V201's evidence, in particular TestCaptureTopUpSession_PostsWalletCreditAtomically (asserts the exact wallet ledger balance after capture), TestAuthorizeTopUpSession_AmbiguousProviderErrorOpensReconciliationCase (asserts exactly one open reconciliation case, no retry), and TestCompleteGovernedRefundWithProvider_CodCollectedSourceBlockedFromRail (asserts zero provider calls, zero ledger transactions for a blocked non-provider-backed source).

deviations.description: VERIFICATION.json's V202 referenced `rg`, which is not installed in this environment. Corrected to the exact-equivalent `grep -rn -E` (recursive, line-numbered, extended-regex, same target path and pattern) before Freeze, documented in VERIFICATION.json's deviationFromOriginalCommand field for V202 -- same class of pre-existing package authoring defect as U001's V103.

services/wlt/backend/cmd/wlt-api/main.go:52 hard-codes `wltHttp.NewRouter(db, mutationsEnabled, nil)` -- no wallet.DecisionService is wired into the running wlt-api-runtime container at all, in any environment, via any env var. internal/wallet/circuit_breaker.go's EnforceKillSwitch fails closed when the DecisionService is nil, so every financial mutation HTTP endpoint in the currently deployed container -- pre-existing endpoints and this unit's new topup-sessions/refund-rail-routing endpoints alike -- unconditionally returns 403 KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this unit's delta: the smoke script's first call (POST /wlt/payment-sessions, an order-payment session, code untouched by U002) already fails identically. Not fixed here: wiring a real DecisionService (e.g. GrowthBook-backed) is an infrastructure/wiring change with no code present anywhere in this repository to adapt, well outside U002's task boundary (CashInRail/ProviderRegistry/FinancialRailRouter/Cash-In engine/refund routing). Flagged for whoever owns wlt-api-runtime's production wiring; reopen trigger is any future unit that needs a real HTTP-level financial-mutation smoke test to pass in this environment.

internal/health/health.go's wltLatestMigration constant (which gates /wlt/readiness AND sqlRuntimeReadinessStore.Ready()) was hard-coded to 'wlt-905_dispatch_financial_eligibility_decisions.sql', already three migrations stale before this unit even started (U001 shipped wlt-908/909/910 without updating it). internal/health/health_test.go's TestReadinessMigrationMatchesGovernedManifestSet exists specifically to catch this drift by reading manifest.json at runtime and comparing it to the constant -- but it silently kept reporting a cached PASS through both U001 and this unit's first `go test ./...` runs, because Go's test cache does not treat a file read via os.ReadFile at test runtime as a cache-invalidating input: once the health package's own source and compiled dependencies are unchanged, `go test` replays the last cached result even though the manifest.json content it reads has since changed underneath it. This means readiness has been silently under-gating since U001 shipped: an operator could have observed /wlt/readiness=ready (and sqlRuntimeReadinessStore.Ready()=true) after only wlt-905 was applied, without wlt-908's financial_purpose/allocation-conservation schema, wlt-909's fail-closed account taxonomy, or wlt-910's opening-balance account actually existing. Caught only because this unit's Freeze adversarial pass ran `go test ./... -count=1` (forcing a full cache bypass) instead of trusting the default cached result. Root-cause fixed by updating the constant to 'wlt-911_payment_topup_source_and_purpose.sql' rather than only patching the test's expectation -- confirmed against the live schema_migrations table (wlt-911 present, success=true, dirty=false) and re-verified with a second full `-count=1` run, all 18 packages PASS. Recorded here rather than silently folded into 'implementation' because it is a pre-existing defect this unit found and fixed, not one it introduced.
